coverage.category: 19. Market traders, street vendors, money changers

coverage.category: 21. Fuel stations and fuel or LPG distributors
coverage.found: SEYPEC is the sole LPG supplier and runs most retail stations (2020 Nation article). Petroleum storage and sale licences fall under SI 19 of 1987. Retailer base is tiny and state-dominated. Nothing to build.

coverage.found: No commodity trading sector of note in Seychelles.

coverage.found: Searches found the Medical Practitioners and Dentists Act, the Health Professionals Act and a Hospitals and Dispensaries Act, but no insurer or state-scheme billing duty and no Health Care Agency facility rules. SI 61 of 2026 amends the Health Professionals schedule. Nothing found.

coverage.category: 28. Notaries, land agents, real estate brokers and other professionals with periodic or anti-money-laundering reports

Seychelles Tourism Board Bill 2026 was approved in March 2026 but deals with marketing. An SNA piece on cracking down on unlicensed accommodation was blocked (403).

coverage.found: See C01.

coverage.found: See C02. The SMSA took over maritime licensing in February 2023. Hire craft need an annual survey, an HC number on the bow, and insurance.

coverage.found: See C06.

coverage.found: SI 37 of 2026 (Radio Communication Equipment Dealer Licence), SI 55 of 2026 (gambling licence grant) and SI 42 of 2026 (Seychelles Made certification) were seen as titles only. Each is a very small buyer group. Nothing to build.

coverage.category: 16. Cemeteries, burial societies and funeral services

coverage.category: 17. Community and religious bodies: associations, charities, halal and kosher supervision
coverage.found: Real duty found: Associations Act 2022 (Act 8/2022, assented 28 Apr 2022, in force 14 Aug 2023 by SI 54/2023 except s.25(3)-(9),(12)-(15) and s.28(1); text confirmed by reading the Act PDF). Secretary must file officer list plus audited accounts before 31 July each year (s.15; fine up to SCR500 for first 60 days, then SCR100 per day), notify officer or office changes within 14 days, and pay annual fee SCR200 by 31 Dec (SCR100 per month penalty). Existing associations had to re-register (six months, up to twelve), then comply within twelve months of the continuation certificate or be cancelled. Registrar can cancel for breaches of the AML/CFT and Beneficial Ownership Acts. Logged as a candidate. Halal and kosher supervision not seen; the Muslim population is small.

coverage.category: 23. Co-operatives, credit unions and savings groups
coverage.found: Co-operatives Act 1987 (SeyLII consolidated to 2012): the management committee chairman must send the Minister monthly activity reports and an annual report, committees meet quarterly, and accounts are audited by a Minister-appointed person. The Seychelles Credit Union is the only credit union and has been supervised by the Central Bank of Seychelles since 31 May 2004; only a handful of co-operatives are active. Logged as a weak candidate.

result.reason: The Act exists (Act 25 of 2022, gazetted 12 Dec 2022). Part III covers childminder registration, renewal, centre licences and a register, and Part IV covers inspection and revocation. I could not confirm the claim's "in force 1 Jan 2023". SeyLII's page is marked "Not commenced", and I found no commencement notice. The gazette PDF was unreadable. A page tied to IECD reports Cabinet approved three sets of regulations around June 2026 (centre standards, home standards, licence conditions). I could not read SI 64-67, so renewal period, fees, penalties and record duties are unchecked. IECD already runs the register and a directory, and I found no competing software. The market is tiny: 27 centres in 2019, and the childminder count was not found. Buyers are small, so willingness to pay is low and the product is a thin checklist and document pack.

Duty looks real: the Control of Hire Craft Act requires a survey before licence grant, and the Boat Charter Policy 2019 sets HC numbers. SMSA took over maritime licensing in 2023 (SI 5 of 2023). I found no SMSA online portal and no Seychelles-specific competitor. Only generic tools turned up (Fleet Rabbit, GoCanvas, DivePlannerPro). The "once per calendar year" survey rule and the penalty were not confirmed in the text I saw. The Act's hire craft definition is narrow (fishing or pleasure hire). Operator count was not found, likely a few hundred. A tiny market with a regulator-driven, paper-based process means low willingness to pay and hard distribution. The score stays low.

Duty is real: the Employment Department FAQ cites Employment Act 1995 s.77(3) for an SR 400 per day late-renewal surcharge. It also cites an SR 40,000 fine for working without a valid GOP (s.77(2)) and deportation risk. The Immigration Department advises employers to apply 6 weeks before expiry. No commercial Seychelles GOP/quota tracker turned up, and no online employer portal was confirmed. The government runs an internal expiry-alert system, not an employer tool. The market is tiny: Seychelles is a small economy, and employer counts were not found. Renewals are in person and infrequent per employer, so a calendar reminder largely substitutes. Agency annual-accounts duty was not re-verified. Willingness to pay is low and the market is very small.

decisions.reason: Childminders and nursery managers with ECD Act registration, renewal and inspections; no known idea covers it.
Hire craft and charter owners with annual survey and licence duty; differs from K02 (guesthouse TESL levy), so it is a new buyer and duty.
Small employers with recurring GOP renewals and quota limits, plus employment agencies; no known idea covers it.
Households as employers under the 2019 domestic worker regulations; in scope. Verifiers can check the contents.
Small controllers with a statutory record-keeping duty under the 2023 Data Protection Act; in scope and not covered by any known idea.
Small licensed money changers with returns and AML record duties; the buyer pool is small but 'few buyers' is for verifiers to judge.
Small professional offices (agents, notaries, dealers) carrying AML/CFT duties; in scope, still unverified.
Small food businesses with approval and inspection duties under the Food Act; no known idea covers it.
Small-scale fishers with licence, registration and logbook duties; K03 covers industrial export traceability, which is a different buyer and duty.
Waste collectors with a record-keeping duty; in scope, unverified.
Pig keepers and pesticide dealers with licence duties; low score but unchecked, so keep for verification.
